did: Home can now hand a video essay the pictures of a walk through one of our apps. When a cards essay names a walk scene, home fetches that run's walks bundle from Snips Capture, checks it whole, and gives the render each named walk's record and pictures. It does this as the third member of the same fetcher that already brings in snips and public pages: the same queue, the same limits and the same five-minute pass. A scene whose run, app or steps home can't give is refused walk-gone, and a scene that names nothing a capture makes, or no token, is refused walk-missing. Codex found that several step ranges of one walk loaded its pictures several times; that is fixed, and each walk is now read once per essay.

calls.title: Where walks sit in the shared fetch queue
options: Pages, then walks, then snips, among keys of the same standing
calls.why: A walks bundle lives a day and a new run means a new cut list, so it goes ahead of snips, which are a re-run away under the same commit. A page can't be taken again at all, so it stays first. Keys whose fetch failed still take turns whatever their family, so none starves another.
calls.undo: Change Family::first in apps/servers/file_host/src/snips.rs and the C1470 call in docs/snips.md.

calls.title: A walk is handed whole, not just the steps a scene shows
options: Hand every picture the walk's record lists
Hand only the named steps, with a trimmed record
calls.why: The render re-checks every picture its record lists, and the record stays exactly as the capture wrote it. A walk is at most 99 pictures, and it is read once per essay.
calls.undo: Trim the record and pictures in essay_media::walks::given and say so in C1472 in docs/snips.md; the render's --walks would need to accept a trimmed record.

left: Two test gaps from the last review, not pushed: no test at the hand() level that two step ranges of one walk read its pictures once, and no test where a walk's first scene waits or is refused and a later one is held. The code is correct for both today.
Walks reach home only after the next server release and deploy, and the client half lands in some-ui #3486 and then #3485.
